abstract: Tool-using research systems can produce an answer and a detailed execution trace while leaving unresolved who executed the work, which evidence was available, whether agreeing runs were independent, and whether infrastructure failure was admitted as scientific evidence. We define a fail-closed execution contract that separates request identity, result integrity, executor attribution, evidence admission and scientific authority. Frozen bounded studies test that separation. The artifact checker rejects all six registered committed-artifact corruptions and accepts all six semantics-preserving re-encodings. At fixed three-link length, one compromised key domain permits four of four forged chains, whereas two or three independent cryptographic domains permit none. Full key-set compromise remains the decisive adverse control: signatures detect zero of six forgeries and an unscoped chain-as-science rule false-promotes all six. A 22-case W3C PROV and RO-Crate/Workflow-Run study preserves the normalized execution vector without leaking scientific fields, and native/imported status interpretation agrees on 22/22. Process-kill tests show that a valid stale artifact can remain green after the current invocation fails, so liveness requires a separate occurrence binding. These are finite execution-integrity, provenance and attestation results, not a general reliability, key-custody, production-scale, or scientific-truth claim.
title: Fail-Closed Research Execution: Receipt Semantics and Independence Contracts
